cur:objects-leipzig-grassi-crucifixion-i.summary: Beneath an arch, Christ hangs on the cross with a large halo, his head bowed and his long body gently swaying; the Virgin raises her hand in grief at the left, while St John stands at the right, his hand to his cheek. The restrained composition gives the Crucifixion the stillness of an icon.
facts: Byzantine crucifixion ivories of the later 10th century often show Christ's body in a gentle curve with the head inclined in death, a type that spread to the West (type).

walters:71.377.summary: The Virgin stands in flowing drapery, holding the Christ Child upright on her left arm as he sits facing outward. Her right hand once held an object, perhaps a flower, now lost. The ivory statuette, mounted on a dark base, continues a conservative devotional type into the 18th century.
facts: The Walters describes the Virgin's features as French, while noting that the drapery has parallels in 17th-century works.
walters:71.377.notes: The worklist year (900) was wrong; the museum dates the figure to the 1st quarter of the 18th century. Image viewed on the Walters image server.
